h: The Final Redemption Leaves No Soul Behind

p: סִיּוּם הַפְטוֹרָה דְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ (יְשַׁעְיָה נב, יב)
The close of this parashah's haftorah (Yeshayahu 52:12):
"For you shall not go out in haste,
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 94b):
"'She shall not go out as the slaves go out' (Shemos 21:7).
that they will go out like those
from the side of the slave,
who went out of Egypt in flight
'she shall not go out as the slaves go out';
And this is because it enumerates there
the levels of nefesh, ruach, neshamah:
that one merits a nefesh from Asiyah,
from the side of the only daughter, etc.;
from the side of the middle pillar,
וְאִקְרֵי בֵּן לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
and he is called a son to HaKadosh Baruch Hu, etc.;
from the side of Abba and Imma, etc.,
when a person merits a nefesh
from the side of the only daughter,
'she shall not go out as the slaves go out.'"
(סוֹף הַקְדָּמָה כז, ב; בִּדְפוּס וִילְנָא טו, א)
(Tikkunei Zohar, end of the Introduction, 27b; Vilna edition 15a)
the Daughter will not go out
is with her in the final exile, etc.;
And because they did not yet have
that the redemption be in haste,
"For they were driven out of Egypt"
that had they delayed any longer,
they were not yet worthy of being redeemed,
And this is what is said in the Tikkunim there:
that regarding the future redemption it says:
"For you shall not go out in haste,
which is called the Name Havayah,
for the blessing over the Torah before it,
"When I call the Name of Hashem,
"And the God of Yisrael will be your rear guard";
"And the banner of the camp of Dan traveled,
the rear guard of all the camps," etc.;
it would return it to him.
And this is the matter of this consolation,
along the lines of what we said
regarding the consolation "Comfort, comfort My people":
that the main purpose of the exiles
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּסַיֵּים שָׁם הַהַפְטוֹרָה (יְשַׁעְיָה מ, כו)
"And the God of Yisrael will be your rear guard,"
for He is the rear guard of all the camps;
that is, that no Jewish soul
And this is the reason for
and even in the present, in exile,
And we say the consolation on Shabbos,
from the side of the only daughter,
and "she shall not go out as the slaves go out,"
as is written in the holy Zohar
and in the Tikkunim cited above.
is called one who engages in Torah;
"For you shall not go out in haste," etc.,

From the Haste of Egypt to Torah Freedom
